name: fheroes2
desc: Recreation of the Heroes of Might and Magic II game engine
why: An open-source engine recreating Heroes of Might and Magic II, a classic strategy game worth playing and studying how the original was reimplemented.

brief.what_it_is: fheroes2 is an open-source, multiplatform recreation of the Heroes of Might and Magic II game engine, written from scratch in C++ according to the README's wording (the README itself does not name the language). It takes the original game's resource files (ANIM, DATA, MAPS and MUSIC folders from a legally purchased copy or the free demo) and runs the game on its own engine. The README says it adds high-resolution graphics, an improved AI, bug fixes and interface improvements. The Homebrew formula installs three executables: fheroes2 (the game), fheroes2-extract-resources (pulls resources from a purchased copy) and fheroes2-install-demo (downloads the demo's files).
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the project is meant to reproduce the original game 'with significant improvements in gameplay, graphics and logic' and to breathe 'new life into one of the most addictive turn-based strategy games.'
brief.how_it_works: The engine is a separate program that does not ship the original game's data. The user supplies the original resource folders, either by running the extraction script on a purchased install (GOG installer or CD) or by running the demo downloader, and then the engine loads them. The README also mentions a full list of changes on a GAME_IMPROVEMENTS page, which I did not open.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew is the path the formula and the INSTALL guide cover. After brew install, the caveats say to run fheroes2-install-demo for the free demo's files, or fheroes2-extract-resources if you own a copy of the game. The caveats also point to a README.txt inside the Cellar at share/doc/fheroes2, for version 1.1.17. The game cannot run without the original resource folders (ANIM, DATA, MAPS, MUSIC), and the guide says these must be gathered before the game works. For manual installs on macOS the destination is ~/.fheroes2, or ~/Library/Application Support/fheroes2 for the native app build. The Linux Homebrew guide says to copy them to $XDG_DATA_HOME/fheroes2 (usually ~/.local/share/fheroes2). Other platforms also have installers, Flatpak, AUR, Gentoo and Windows options, and the Windows ZIP build may need Microsoft Visual C++ redistributables.
brief.standout: The engine is a clean-room reimplementation that refuses to include the original data, so the user has to supply it from a legal copy or the free demo. The project also ships scripts for the demo download and resource extraction, which is an unusual way to make a remake that depends on closed assets.
brief.status: unknown. The README and homepage are current and link to a working installation guide, Discord, Patreon/PayPal/Boosty, and CI and SonarCloud badges. Homebrew lists version 1.1.17. I did not see a last commit or release date, so I cannot confirm how recently the project has been updated.
brief.caveats: The original game data is not included. You need a purchased copy (GOG or Ubisoft Store recommended by the project) or the English-only free demo. The project says it does not support illegal use of the original game. The source is GPL v2. The macOS ZIP build is x86-64 only, so Apple Silicon users should use Homebrew or MacPorts or build from source. Some platforms (PlayStation Vita, Nintendo Switch) need custom firmware. The README calls the 'latest commit' snapshot binaries 'mainly intended for developers' that might not work properly. I did not read the GAME_IMPROVEMENTS page or the FAQ, so I cannot say what features are missing. The brew caveats point to a README.txt that I did not fetch.

entry.title: fheroes2
entry.tldr: An open-source engine that runs Heroes of Might and Magic II from its original data files, with higher resolution and a better AI.
entry.deeper_look:
fheroes2 is a from-scratch reimplementation of the engine behind Heroes of Might and Magic II, the 1990s turn-based strategy game. It reads the original game's resource folders (ANIM, DATA, MAPS and MUSIC) and runs the game on new code. The README says it adds high-resolution graphics, an improved AI, bug fixes and interface improvements.

The project does not ship the original art, maps or music. You supply them yourself, either from a legally purchased copy (the project recommends GOG or the Ubisoft Store) or from the free, English-only demo. The formula installs two helper scripts for this: one downloads the demo files, the other extracts resources from a purchased install.

The idea underneath is the engine remake: take a closed game, rewrite the code that runs it, and leave the copyrighted assets with the person who owns them. The code is GPL v2, and the README says it does not support illegal use of the original game. It is a way to see how a classic game's rules and data formats can be rebuilt by outsiders, and a good excuse to play a classic.

The README describes the goal as reproducing the original "with significant improvements in gameplay, graphics and logic". A full list of changes lives in the repository's GAME_IMPROVEMENTS page.
entry.install:
brew install fheroes2
# then, for the free demo files:
fheroes2-install-demo
# or, if you own the original game:
fheroes2-extract-resources
# The game will not start without the original resource folders.

try_this.what_happens: Downloads and installs the files from the original game's free demo so the engine has data to load.
Extracts the needed resource files from a legally purchased copy of the original game, such as a GOG installer or CD.

entry.whats_unique: It is a remake that deliberately ships none of the original data, and it provides scripts to fetch the demo or extract files from a copy you own.
entry.caveats: The original game data is not included, and the free demo is English-only; the brief could not confirm when the project last had a commit or release.
